data.title: Proportional Reasoning: Recipes, Rates, and Scientific Ratios
data.description: Engage in advanced proportional reasoning across real-world scenarios including culinary scaling, retail economics, kinematic speed calculations, and chemical solution preparation. Analyze equivalent ratios and derive unit rates to solve complex missing-value problems.

challenges.instruction: A classic artisan sourdough recipe utilizes a base ratio of 4 cups of unbleached flour to 1.5 cups of filtered water. If you scale up the production to yield a larger batch requiring 6 cups of water, how many cups of flour must you incorporate to maintain the exact structural hydration ratio?
challenges.hint: Determine the scalar factor by comparing your target water to the base water amount, then apply that same factor to the flour.

challenges.instruction: Bulk purchasing analysis reveals a wholesale pricing structure where 3 kilograms of organic coffee beans cost $42.75. Operating under this constant unit rate, what will be the total cost required to acquire a commercial supply of 7.5 kilograms?
challenges.hint: Calculate the unit price per single kilogram first, or find the combined multiplier linking 3 kg to 7.5 kg.

challenges.instruction: During a deep-space telemetry test, a probe maintains a constant velocity traveling 125.5 miles in 2.5 hours. At this unwavering cruise velocity, how many total miles will the probe traverse if the observation window extends to 6 hours?
challenges.hint: Find the unit rate of miles per hour by dividing the distance by the hours, then multiply by the new time duration.

challenges.instruction: In a biochemical laboratory experiment, a neutralizing aqueous solution requires a strict mixing ratio of 5 milliliters of acid concentrate to 12.5 milliliters of distilled water. If a researcher measures out precisely 14 milliliters of acid concentrate, how many milliliters of distilled water are needed to preserve chemical equilibrium?
challenges.hint: Determine the multiplier by dividing the new amount of acid by the base amount of acid (14 divided by 5).
